text:
Dylan Holloway was one of the stories of last season in St. Louis, the offer-sheet signing who turned into a 22-goal winger in 59 games and, by Evolving-Hockey's count, the 20th most valuable forward in the league. This season the line with Robert Thomas and Jimmy Snuggerud has been reunited, and Mike Fink of The Hockey News called it the Blues' line to watch.

His own goals haven't come along yet. He has three in 17 games on 4.2 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 7.9%, below what we'd expect, and our win model has his goals near the bottom of the league in wins added. The rest of his game is fine: 12 points, a 95th percentile top speed, and the Blues are about four points better in 5v5 expected-goal share with him on than without. Evolving-Hockey did warn that last season's results ran ahead of his chances, so some regression was always coming. Our projection has 17 to 32 more goals. Snuggerud is getting the goals on that line; Holloway's should follow.
headline: Holloway is waiting on his goals
